memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not degrade your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with wickedness. Observe my Sabbaths and have reverence for my sanctuary. I am the LORD.'" - Lev 19:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A father might do this out of poverty, or greed, or because his neighbours did. God calls it what it is: degrading your daughter.

The word matters. Not "using" her, not "employing" her — degrading. God names the act by what it does to her worth.

And notice the consequence He warns of. It does not stop with one family. The land will turn to prostitution and be filled with wickedness. What one father does in his household spreads until it shapes a whole society.

This remains one of the great evils of our world. Millions of women and girls are trafficked and exploited, and it happens because there is money in it and because people look away. God does not look away. He sees every one of them.

Then, remarkably, the next line is about Sabbath and sanctuary. Worship and justice sit side by side, as they always do in Scripture. A people who exploit their daughters cannot claim to honour God on the Sabbath. Isaiah thundered this: stop doing wrong. Learn to do right; seek justice. Defend the oppressed (Isa 1:16-17).

Real worship and real justice have never been separable.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you keep worship and justice connected, or treat them separately?
2. What are you aware of in the world that you have chosen not to look at?
3. How could you support work that protects the exploited?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see every exploited woman and girl, and You do not look away. Give me eyes that see, a heart that cares, and hands willing to act. Amen.
